what
The repo is the Memos Go + React app (github.com/usememos/memos). There is no `benchmark_tests/`, `bench/`, `benchmark/`, `tests/`, or `e2e/` directory anywhere in this workspace, hidden or otherwise. The complete benchmark/test harness is a hidden `.bench/` directory with exactly three files: `serve_memos.py` (immutable app fixture launcher), `validate_answer.py` (public answer-format validator, no expected answers), and `navigation-answer.schema.json` (JSON Schema for the same answer format). There are no examples of "benchmark tests" beyond these three files, and no repo references to `browser_open`, `browser_screenshot`, `browser_console`, `browser_network`, or `/opt/benchmark-public/browser_check.py`. The only `/opt/benchmark*` reference is `.bench/serve_memos.py` invoking the backend binary at `/opt/benchmark/memos`.

  - `.bench/serve_memos.py`
  - `.bench/validate_answer.py`
  - `.bench/navigation-answer.schema.json`
- `web/package.json` — frontend scripts (`dev`, `build`, `release`, `lint`)
- `web/vite.config.ts` — dev server port and API proxy config
- `web/src/router/index.tsx` — route table containing `/reader`
- `web/src/pages/Reader.tsx` — `/reader` page component
- `web/src/lib/reader.ts` — data loading used by `/reader`
- `store/migration/sqlite/LATEST.sql` — schema file serve_memos.py executes to seed SQLite
- `.github/workflows/backend-tests.yml` — regular Go test CI (go test ./...)
- `store/test/` and `plugin/.../*_test.go` — regular Go unit tests only; not a benchmark harness

facts
1) `benchmark_tests/` location/structure/naming: does not exist. Verified by targeted searches of `benchmark_tests`, `benchmark-tests`, `bench`, `tests`, `e2e`, and `benchmark`. No such directory. The equivalent is the hidden `.bench/` directory; its naming convention is the answer file `navigation-answer.json` (default CLI input) plus a `-answer.schema.json` schema and a `serve_*.py` fixture launcher. There is no task-spec file or runner script for individual "tests".

2) Existing example files (the only ones that exist):

`.bench/validate_answer.py` in full, CLI and validation logic:

`.bench/navigation-answer.schema.json` key rules:
- top-level object, `additionalProperties: false`, `required: ["task_id","symbols","edges","claims"]`
- `task_id`: `type: string`
- `symbols`: array of objects, each `additionalProperties: false`, `required: ["path","name"]`; `path` `pattern: "^(?!/)(?!.*\\.\\.).+"`; `name` `minLength: 1` with description:
  `"Use Class.member for methods and Class.#private for private methods; function or class names otherwise. Bare member names are accepted when unambiguous in the cited file."`
- `edges`: array of objects, `required: ["from","to"]`, both `type: string`
- `claims`: object map `string -> string`, each value `minLength: 1`

3) `.bench/serve_memos.py` (full 22 lines already read). Behavior:
- Seeds a SQLite DB at `/tmp/memos-data/memos_prod.db` only if it does not exist.
- Executes the repo schema `store/migration/sqlite/LATEST.sql`, then inserts:
  - `INSERT INTO migration_history(version) VALUES ('0.24.4')`
  - `INSERT INTO user(id,username,role,nickname,password_hash) VALUES (1,'reader','HOST','Reader','unused')`
  - memo id 1, uid `alpha`, creator_id 1, `PUBLIC`, created/updated 1700000000 with content computed as:
    `"# Alpha release\n\n#release \n\n" + "VeryLongMemo"*80 + "\n\n| Name | State |\n| --- | --- |\n| Alpha | Ready |\n\n```python\nprint('ready')\n```"`
  - memo id 2, uid `beta`, content `"# Beta planning\n\n#planning Next steps"`, `PUBLIC`, created/updated 1700000010
  - `INSERT INTO resource(id,uid,creator_id,filename,type,size,memo_id,storage_type,reference) VALUES(1,'attachment',1,?,'application/pdf',100,1,'EXTERNAL','https://example.com/report.pdf')` with filename `('quarterly-report-'*20+'.pdf')`
- Starts the backend:
  `subprocess.Popen(['/opt/benchmark/memos','--mode','prod','--data',str(data),'--port','8081'])`
  so the backend serves on `http://127.0.0.1:8081`.
- Waits for readiness by polling `http://127.0.0.1:8081/api/v1/memos` up to 120 times, 0.5 s apart.
- Then starts the frontend:
  `subprocess.Popen(['npm','run','dev','--','--host','127.0.0.1'], cwd='web')`
  and calls `frontend.wait()`. In `finally`, `backend.terminate()`.
- Frontend port: `web/package.json` `"dev": "vite"`; `web/vite.config.ts` sets `server.port: 3001`, host `0.0.0.0`, and proxies `^/api`, `^/memos.api.v1`, `^/file` to `http://localhost:8081` (overridable by env var `DEV_PROXY_SERVER`).
- How to reach `/reader`: while serve_memos.py is running, the frontend is at `http://127.0.0.1:3001`, so `/reader` is `http://127.0.0.1:3001/reader`. Route is defined in `web/src/router/index.tsx`:
  `{ path: "/reader", element: <Reader /> },`
  `Reader` (web/src/pages/Reader.tsx) loads `loadMemos()` from `web/src/lib/reader.ts`, which fetches `"/api/v1/memos?pageSize=100"` (proxied to port 8081) and renders `memo.name`, `memo.creator`, `memo.displayTime`, `memo.nodes`, and `memo.resources` links.

4) Browser tool references: none. Searches for `browser_open`, `browser_screenshot`, `browser_console`, `browser_network`, `browser_check`, and `/opt/benchmark-public` returned zero matches across non-hidden files; explicit searches inside `.bench/` and `.github/` also returned zero browser references. The only `/opt/benchmark` reference in the whole repo is `.bench/serve_memos.py` line 13 launching `/opt/benchmark/memos`. `/opt/benchmark-public/browser_check.py` is not present and not referenced; it is outside this workspace and read_file only accepts workspace-relative paths, so it could not be inspected.

How a new benchmark test is added and run (given what actually exists):
- The repo has no per-task test runner, test fixtures directory, or test registration mechanism. A "test submission" in this harness is a JSON answer file matching `navigation-answer.schema.json` (keys `task_id`, `symbols`, `edges`, `claims`).
- Validate it with:
  `python3 .bench/validate_answer.py /path/to/answer.json`
  or, using the default `navigation-answer.json`, just:
  `python3 .bench/validate_answer.py`
  Valid input prints `Answer format valid (correctness is not checked).` and exits 0; invalid input prints each error on its own line and exits 1. `validate_answer.py` deliberately has no expected answers; correctness is checked externally, not by this file.
- To exercise the app fixture, run the immutable launcher: it requires `/opt/benchmark/memos` on PATH at that exact path, `npm` deps installed in `web/` (vite), and the repo `store/migration/sqlite/LATEST.sql` relative to the repo root (the script is not chdir-independent). While it runs, the backend API is `http://127.0.0.1:8081/api/...` and the frontend/reader is `http://127.0.0.1:3001/reader`.
- Regular (non-benchmark) Go tests run with `go test -v ./...` as in `.github/workflows/backend-tests.yml`; CI also runs `go mod tidy` diff check and golangci-lint v2.1.6.

verdict
There is no `benchmark_tests/` directory and no browser-check integration in this workspace. The only benchmark harness is the hidden `.bench/` directory: a format validator (`validate_answer.py`) paired with a schema (`navigation-answer.schema.json`), plus an immutable fixture launcher (`serve_memos.py`) that seeds data and boots backend (port 8081) and frontend (port 3001, route `/reader`). A new benchmark test would be a JSON answer file validated by `.bench/validate_answer.py`; there is no local executor for tasks or browser checks.

reasoning
The harness shape matches an agentic "navigation/exploration" benchmark rather than a unit-test suite: a fixed seeded app (`serve_memos.py`) provides a deterministic target, and agents submit a structured `navigation-answer.json` describing the symbols, edges, and claims they found. Validation is deliberately limited to format (`validate_answer.py` has "no expected answers"), so correctness must live in an external grader. That is why a new task requires only an answer JSON conforming to the schema; the app fixture and format checker are already fixed in `.bench/`.

response.text:
what: Made the `/reader` feed responsive in production source only, exactly per the provided design. Extended `web/src/css/reader.css` with mobile-first grid, card overflow/wrap containment, metadata wrapping, attachment wrapping, image bounds, and local code/table scroll. Added a `memo-content-scroll` wrapper class in the CodeBlock and Table JSX so the CSS can target code/table scroll containers without altering non-reader behavior.

paths:
- `web/src/css/reader.css` — replaced the 3-rule file. `.reader-feed` is now `grid; gap:20px; grid-template-columns:minmax(0,1fr)`, with `@media (min-width:1024px) { grid-template-columns:repeat(2, minmax(0,1fr)) }`. Added `min-width:0` and `overflow-wrap:anywhere; word-break:break-word` to `.reader-feed article`. Added `.reader-meta` wrapping/spacing, `.reader-attachments` (flex column, gap, min-width 0, max-width 100%, wrap anywhere) and `.reader-attachments a` rules, scoped `img { max-width:100%; height:auto; }`, and `.reader-feed article .memo-content-scroll { max-width:100%; overflow-x:auto; display:block; }`.
- `web/src/components/MemoContent/CodeBlock.tsx` — inner pre wrapper changed from `<div className="overflow-auto">` to `<div className="memo-content-scroll w-full overflow-auto">`.
- `web/src/components/MemoContent/Table.tsx` — wrapped the existing table in `<div className="memo-content-scroll w-full overflow-x-auto">`; table and row/cell rendering unchanged.

reasoning: The decision points were already made, so I implemented them directly. The key non-obvious choice was the scroll container. `<pre>` could be styled in place, but markdown tables have no wrapper; wrapping both in a shared `.memo-content-scroll` element lets reader.css provide local `overflow-x:auto` for narrow cards while the `pre`/table content keeps its intrinsic fixed width. The class is layout-neutral outside the reader because all styling is scoped under `.reader-feed article`. Attachment links are blockified automatically as flex items in the column-flex `.reader-attachments`, so `max-width:100%`/`min-width:0` actually constrains them and `overflow-wrap:anywhere` wraps the `quarterly-report-…pdf` name. `overflow-wrap:anywhere` (rather than only `break-word`) is important at 375px because browsers consider it when computing min-content size, preventing the unbroken `VeryLongMemo`×80 string from expanding the card/page. I did not touch `Reader.tsx`, `reader.ts`, config, `.bench/`, or any `.go` code, and I did not start the server.

- Separate tester flow: run `python .bench/serve_memos.py`, open `http://127.0.0.1:3001/reader`.
- Expected at 375px viewport: single column; no horizontal page scroll; `VeryLongMemo`×80 wraps instead of overflowing its card; `quarterly-report-…pdf` filename wraps and remains fully visible inside the attachment area; the Python code block scrolls horizontally inside its own card only; the markdown table scrolls horizontally inside its own wrapper only; creator/date text wraps without ellipsis; any reader image is `max-width:100%` with preserved aspect ratio.
- Edge/failure case at 375px: confirm the long attachment name does not push the page wider — that was the main previously unconstrained item.
- Expected at 1280px viewport: `.reader-feed` renders two equal columns via `repeat(2, minmax(0,1fr))`.

what: Made the `/reader` feed responsive in production source only, exactly per the provided design. Extended `web/src/css/reader.css` with mobile-first grid, card overflow/wrap containment, metadata wrapping, attachment wrapping, image bounds, and local code/table scroll. Added a `memo-content-scroll` wrapper class in the CodeBlock and Table JSX so the CSS can target code/table scroll containers without altering non-reader behavior.

paths:
- `web/src/css/reader.css` — replaced the 3-rule file. `.reader-feed` is now `grid; gap:20px; grid-template-columns:minmax(0,1fr)`, with `@media (min-width:1024px) { grid-template-columns:repeat(2, minmax(0,1fr)) }`. Added `min-width:0` and `overflow-wrap:anywhere; word-break:break-word` to `.reader-feed article`. Added `.reader-meta` wrapping/spacing, `.reader-attachments` (flex column, gap, min-width 0, max-width 100%, wrap anywhere) and `.reader-attachments a` rules, scoped `img { max-width:100%; height:auto; }`, and `.reader-feed article .memo-content-scroll { max-width:100%; overflow-x:auto; display:block; }`.
- `web/src/components/MemoContent/CodeBlock.tsx` — inner pre wrapper changed from `<div className="overflow-auto">` to `<div className="memo-content-scroll w-full overflow-auto">`.
- `web/src/components/MemoContent/Table.tsx` — wrapped the existing table in `<div className="memo-content-scroll w-full overflow-x-auto">`; table and row/cell rendering unchanged.

reasoning: The decision points were already made, so I implemented them directly. The key non-obvious choice was the scroll container. `<pre>` could be styled in place, but markdown tables have no wrapper; wrapping both in a shared `.memo-content-scroll` element lets reader.css provide local `overflow-x:auto` for narrow cards while the `pre`/table content keeps its intrinsic fixed width. The class is layout-neutral outside the reader because all styling is scoped under `.reader-feed article`. Attachment links are blockified automatically as flex items in the column-flex `.reader-attachments`, so `max-width:100%`/`min-width:0` actually constrains them and `overflow-wrap:anywhere` wraps the `quarterly-report-…pdf` name. `overflow-wrap:anywhere` (rather than only `break-word`) is important at 375px because browsers consider it when computing min-content size, preventing the unbroken `VeryLongMemo`×80 string from expanding the card/page. I did not touch `Reader.tsx`, `reader.ts`, config, `.bench/`, or any `.go` code, and I did not start the server.
